scope: Delivery track only: take a revision-bound READY task through isolated implementation, author evidence, independent clean-room verification, review, merge-queue integration, terminal status, and resource cleanup. It specifies branch/worktree ownership, exact-head evidence binding, CI/review separation, merge admission, branch/workspace/comment/artifact retention, recovery, and remote Project-status reconciliation. Planning/readiness, deployment, incident intake, and policy self-improvement are inputs or downstream interfaces, not powers of the delivery worker. Desired lifecycle/policy in Git is distinct from actual GitHub Project v2 state: Projects is a mutable remote GraphQL control-plane, so status-as-code means a controller reconciles declared schema/mappings and reports drift; it never treats a YAML edit as proof that a remote item moved (GitHub Projects API: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects). Self-improvement stops at a signed proposal plus evaluation evidence; the author/agent cannot approve its own workflow, permissions, rulesets, required checks, or promotion.
current_capabilities:
GitHub provides the primitives but not the complete transaction. Rulesets can require pull requests, reviews, status checks, signed commits, code scanning, deployments, and merge queues, expose evaluation/bypass behavior, and have REST management APIs; overlapping rulesets aggregate rather than offering a single atomic policy object (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets). Protected branches can dismiss stale approvals, require approval of the most recent push, CODEOWNER review, conversation resolution, status checks, linear history, merge queue, successful deployments, and optionally disallow bypass (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches). A merge queue tests a temporary merge group against the latest base and supports build concurrency 1–100, group size/wait controls, check timeout, and merge method; Actions workflows that supply required checks must subscribe to `merge_group`, or the required result never appears and the merge fails (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#merge_group).

Actions supports job/workflow concurrency, cancellation, artifacts with configurable retention and SHA-256 upload/download digest validation, artifact deletion APIs, dependency review, code scanning, and build provenance attestations (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations; https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependency-review). GitHub-hosted runners are fresh VMs for each job, whereas self-hosted runners do not inherently guarantee a clean image; thus a new job is not sufficient evidence of clean-room execution on a persistent self-host (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/github-hosted-runners; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/self-hosted-runners). `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions are configurable per workflow/job and GitHub recommends least privilege; broader capabilities require a GitHub App installation token or another credential (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/authenticate-with-github_token).

Git supports multiple linked worktrees and explicit `list --porcelain`, `lock`, `remove`, `repair`, and `prune --expire`; worktree metadata is shared with the repository and is not a durable remote lease by itself (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree). REST endpoints can dismiss reviews, delete refs, delete artifacts and workflow runs, while repository setting `delete_branch_on_merge` supports automatic head deletion (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/git/refs; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#update-a-repository). No GitHub primitive atomically commits issue/Project status, PR merge, lease release, branch deletion, and external workspace deletion; an idempotent controller/saga is required.
representative_systems: Recommended reference stack: GitHub Issues/Project v2 as human-visible work index; a GitHub App as controller identity; repository-owned JSON Schemas and workflows; Git worktrees or ephemeral VMs/containers as worker isolation; GitHub rulesets/CODEOWNERS/Actions/merge queue as enforcement; Actions artifacts plus artifact attestations/SLSA provenance as evidence transport; and an external lease/store when multiple workers exist. GitHub Copilot cloud agent is a useful bounded-agent precedent: GitHub says only users with write access can trigger it, it is limited to one branch/simple push operations, draft PRs require human review, and branch protections still apply (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/cloud-agent/risks-and-mitigations). Copilot code review is an advisory reviewer precedent: by default it leaves COMMENT, not APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES, although admins can configure approvals (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/request-a-code-review/use-code-review). OpenSSF Scorecard and `zizmor` are representative policy/static checks for dangerous workflow triggers, token permissions, and unpinned Actions, but neither proves application correctness (https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md; https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor). SLSA v1.2 and NIST SSDF 1.1 provide supply-chain and secure-development control vocabulary rather than a GitHub lifecycle implementation (https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/requirements; https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final).
primary_evidence: Primary findings: (1) merge queue requires CI coverage of the synthesized merge group, not merely the PR head; GitHub explicitly requires the `merge_group` trigger for Actions-based required checks (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue). (2) Approvals can be bound to a diff snapshot by dismissing stale approvals, and the most-recent-push approval option prevents the last pusher from being the sole approving reviewer (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches). (3) Ruleset bypass actors can include roles, teams, and GitHub Apps, so bypass membership is privileged configuration and must be reviewed/audited outside the agent (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets). (4) GitHub calls full-length commit-SHA pinning the only immutable way to reference an Action and recommends treating context values as untrusted input (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use). (5) Artifact upload returns a SHA-256 digest and download validates it, while artifact attestations record build provenance; neither substitutes for retaining the test manifest and exact source/base SHA (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations). (6) Project v2 automation uses GraphQL queries/mutations with `read:project`/`project` or GitHub App permissions and supports webhooks; this proves remote API mutation, not declarative convergence (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects). (7) worktree remove/prune are separate operations with administrative metadata, so deleting a directory directly is incomplete cleanup (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree).
independent_evidence: Counterevidence constrains autonomy. GitHub Security Lab documents the `pull_request_target` + checkout-of-untrusted-PR pattern as capable of leaking secrets or repository write permission; fork content and PR metadata must be treated as hostile (2021-08-03, https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/). Palo Alto Unit 42’s analysis of the 2025 `tj-actions/changed-files` compromise reports a real Action supply-chain incident and shows that marketplace popularity/version tags are not a trust boundary; pin SHAs, minimize tokens/secrets, inspect workflow changes, and retain detection evidence (updated 2025-04-02, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/). BitsAI-CR’s industrial deployment reports 75.0% precision and 26.7% “Outdated Rate” for Go comments, despite 12,000 weekly active users; the missing quarter of precision is strong evidence not to count an AI comment as correctness proof or sole approval (Sun et al., FSE Companion 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15134, DOI https://doi.org/10.1145/3696630.3728552). A 2025 exploratory field study found concern about false positives and preferences that varied with codebase familiarity and review risk, supporting hybrid AI/human review rather than replacement (Aðalsteinsson et al., ESEM 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16339, DOI https://doi.org/10.1109/ESEM64174.2025.00013). NIST SSDF requires defined roles, protected software/components, review/analysis, provenance and vulnerability response, reinforcing separation of duties and retained records (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final). These sources do not measure this proposed end-to-end controller; a pilot must establish local defect, flake, latency, and cleanup baselines.
metrics_and_limits:
Platform facts to encode, not assume: merge-queue build concurrency is configurable from 1 to 100; rulesets are limited to 75 per repository and 75 organization-wide according to current GitHub documentation (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue; https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets). Actions concurrency ordering is not guaranteed; with the default `single` queue, only one pending run remains and a newer run replaces it, while `cancel-in-progress: true` also cancels the running member (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency). Actions service/runtime/rate limits are plan- and runner-dependent and can change; read them dynamically and alert instead of embedding a universal capacity claim (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits). Artifact retention is configurable, and deletion is available through API/UI; policy must choose evidence retention by risk/legal need, not rely on defaults (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts).

Pilot SLOs and denominators: claim-to-workspace p95 <5 min; orphan workspaces after 2×lease TTL = 0; duplicate active claims = 0; evidence manifests with exact head/base SHA, workflow SHA, check-run IDs, artifact digests and verdict = 100%; required checks rerun on `merge_group` = 100%; stale-approval merges = 0; branch/worktree cleanup p95 <24 h after terminal state; cleanup success ≥99% in 24 h and 100% in 7 d or ticket; flaky rerun rate and pass-after-rerun reported separately; escaped-defect and rollback rates per merged PR; human minutes and CI dollars per accepted PR; AI-review findings confirmed/dismissed/outdated by severity. No defensible universal threshold for AI-review accuracy, clean-room cost, merge latency, or safe retry count exists in cited evidence. Start retry cap at one infrastructure retry and zero automatic semantic-failure retries, then tune from labeled local data.
recommended_design:
Use an event-driven, least-privilege delivery saga with five separated identities: controller, implementation worker, verifier, reviewer, merger/cleanup controller. The implementation token may read issue/context and push only `agent/<task-id>/<attempt-id>`; it cannot edit rulesets/workflows on default branch, approve, merge, deploy, change Project schema, or delete audit evidence. Verification starts from a fresh GitHub-hosted VM or attested disposable image, fetches an allowlisted commit, verifies `head_sha`, checks no undeclared generated/untracked output, installs from a lockfile without author caches, and uses no write token or production secrets. Required results attach to the exact PR head; merge queue repeats the required subset against `merge_group` and latest base (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue).

Make the evidence bundle machine-readable and content-addressed: `evidence.json` includes schema version, task/revision/attempt/PR, repository, base/head/merge-group SHA, toolchain/container/workflow/action SHAs, commands, check-run IDs and URLs, test counts/results, regression base-fail/candidate-pass proof, scanners/SBOM/license/dependency results, changed paths and risk, artifact names/digests/attestation IDs, reviewer verdicts, timestamps and redactions. Sign/attest releasable artifacts and preserve immutable summaries even when large logs expire (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations; https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/requirements).

Treat `.github/project-os/project.yaml` as desired field/status/mapping policy and Project v2 as observed remote state. A reconciler reads both, produces a dry-run diff, applies only allowlisted additive/known-ID mutations with optimistic preconditions, records old/new snapshots and request/event IDs, then reads back. Unknown fields/statuses, destructive changes, permissions/ruleset drift, or ambiguous item identity produce `DRIFT_BLOCKED` and human approval; never silently overwrite. Issue/PR truth derives from GitHub IDs and SHAs; Project status is a projection. Webhook delivery IDs are deduplicated, but periodic full reconciliation repairs missed/out-of-order events (Projects API/webhooks: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects).
state_and_event_contract:
States: `READY -> CLAIMED -> PROVISIONING -> EXECUTING -> PROPOSED -> VERIFYING -> REVIEWING -> MERGE_READY -> QUEUED -> MERGED -> CLEANING -> DONE`; side states `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`, `CANCELED`, `SUPERSEDED`, `VERIFY_FAILED`, `MERGE_FAILED`, `DRIFT_BLOCKED`, `CLEANUP_PENDING`, `ESCALATED`. `DONE` means merge or explicit no-change closure plus verified cleanup; it is not synonymous with closed PR.

Every command/event carries `event_id`, GitHub delivery/run/check IDs when present, `task_id`, `task_revision`, `attempt_id`, `lease_fence`, `repo_id`, `pr_number`, `base_ref`, `base_sha`, `head_sha`, `actor`, `from`, `to`, `occurred_at`, `reason`, and `evidence_uri/digest`. The durable journal has a unique `(source,event_id)` key; transition compare-and-swap requires expected state, revision, head SHA and fencing token. Duplicate events return the prior outcome. Stale head/revision/lease events are recorded but cannot advance. Out-of-order events trigger read-after-write reconciliation against PR/check/ruleset/Project state.

Key triggers: lease acquired -> provision; push/synchronize -> invalidate prior evidence/approval and verify new head; required check completion -> recompute predicate, never accept a check from another SHA; review submission/dismissal -> recompute review predicate; `merge_group` -> execute queue workflow on group SHA; merged/closed -> revoke lease and enqueue cleanup; TTL/heartbeat miss -> cancel, revoke credentials, preserve diagnostics, mark stale, and optionally requeue with a new attempt. Merge predicate = exact current head + current task revision + nonexpired lease + allowed diff/risk + required clean-room checks + required CODEOWNER/human approvals + resolved conversations + no blocking drift + queue eligibility. GitHub’s stale-approval and merge-queue semantics are enforcement backstops (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#merge_group). Cleanup is its own retryable saga, never rollback of a successful merge.
repository_artifacts:
Minimum exact tree: `.github/project-os/project.schema.json` and `project.yaml` (desired Project fields/status IDs or stable aliases, allowed transitions, observed-state ownership, destructive-change policy); `lifecycle.schema.json` and `lifecycle.yaml`; `risk.schema.json`/`risk.yaml`; `permissions.yaml` (identity-to-GitHub-App/workflow permissions); `review-policy.yaml`; `cleanup-policy.yaml` (terminal-state matrix, TTLs, deletion/retention/redaction/legal-hold rules); `evidence.schema.json`; `events.schema.json`; `reconciler.yaml`; `.github/CODEOWNERS`; `.github/pull_request_template.md`; `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, `merge-group.yml`, `policy-check.yml`, `cleanup.yml`, `reconcile-project.yml`, and reusable pinned workflows under `.github/workflows/`; `scripts/bootstrap-worktree`, `verify-clean-room`, `build-evidence`, `reconcile-project`, `cleanup-attempt`, and `audit`; lockfiles; toolchain versions; `docs/runbooks/{stale-lease,merge-queue,cleanup,drift,security-incident}.md`; `tests/policy/`, `tests/contracts/`, `tests/fixtures/webhooks/`, and protected regression fixtures.

Pin third-party Actions by full commit SHA and record upstream tag in a comment; GitHub says a full SHA is the only immutable Action reference (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use). Store schemas and desired policy in Git, but do not commit short-lived leases, raw secrets, mutable check verdicts, or Project item status as if declarative truth. The event journal and observed snapshots live in an append-only external store/artifact index with GitHub IDs/digests; the Project board remains a reconciled view. Workflow changes, CODEOWNERS, permissions, cleanup retention, risk gates, evaluation baselines, and promoter identity are protected paths requiring independent human owners.
workflow_steps:
1. Controller re-reads issue/task revision and desired/observed policy; stop on ambiguity, drift, dependency or risk gate. 2. Atomically claim with lease/fencing token and idempotency key; project `READY->CLAIMED` is reconciled/read back, not assumed. 3. Create one branch and one registered worktree/disposable VM; record base SHA/image/toolchain; mint a short-lived branch-scoped credential. 4. Implement within path/command/network/diff budgets; never expose production secrets; checkpoint on cancellation. 5. Push and open/update a draft PR whose body links task revision and evidence manifest; one active attempt per task. 6. Destroy authoring environment access, then verifier checks out exact head into a new clean environment, restores only audited immutable dependencies, and runs format/lint/type/unit/integration/contract/security/secret/dependency/license/SBOM plus policy tests. A bug regression must fail on base and pass on candidate. 7. Upload redacted evidence, verify artifact digest, and attest releasable output (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations). Stop on semantic failure; allow at most one labeled infrastructure retry.

8. AI review may triage or comment but may not satisfy required approval during baseline/pilot; an independent human/CODEOWNER reviews exact head, risk, evidence, architecture and test adequacy. New pushes dismiss/rebind approval (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches). 9. Controller recomputes merge predicate and marks `MERGE_READY`; merger admits only via protected auto-merge/merge queue. 10. `merge_group` workflow rebuilds/tests the synthesized head against latest base; fail/timeout removes or blocks per policy and creates diagnosis evidence, never bypass (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue). 11. On merge webhook, confirm merged SHA/repository, write terminal audit record, update issue/Project by compare-and-set and read back. 12. Revoke tokens/lease, remove registered worktree then prune metadata, delete ephemeral workspace/cache, delete head ref if safe, minimize bot comments, and apply artifact/log retention. REST supports ref/artifact deletion (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/git/refs; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts); Git defines worktree remove/prune (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree). 13. Sweep periodically for orphan refs/worktrees/runs/comments/leases and open cleanup incidents on exhausted retries.
human_gates:
Humans are mandatory for: initial policy/ruleset/App-permission/CODEOWNERS and retention approval; any workflow or dependency capable of receiving secrets/write tokens; destructive Project schema reconciliation; ruleset bypass or exception; ambiguous/expanded scope; security/auth/crypto/billing/privacy/data migration/public API/production/IaC or high-blast-radius changes; generated code with unverifiable source; failing/waived checks; secret exposure; and promotion of agent prompts/tools/evals/policies. Bind approval to `task_revision + head_sha + policy_version + evidence_digest + risk_tier`; any new push, task acceptance change, material policy drift, or evidence replacement invalidates it. Enable stale-review dismissal and most-recent-push approval, require CODEOWNER for protected paths, require conversation resolution, and disallow broad bypass (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches).

AI review is additive. During pilot its verdict is COMMENT-only and cannot fill required approvals, consistent with Copilot’s default behavior (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/request-a-code-review/use-code-review). Later use as a required *check* only after local calibrated evaluation, with a human still required for R2/R3 and protected paths. An exception record requires human approver outside the author/controller, exact scope/SHA, reason, compensating controls, expiry, linked incident, and post-review. No agent may approve its own code, modify the gate that judges its change, approve a self-improvement proposal, or promote the evaluator/prompt/tool it authored.
security_and_failure_modes:
Threats and controls: prompt injection in issue/code/test output -> treat all repository content as data, fixed tool allowlist, network deny/allowlist, no production secrets, and no policy override through content; malicious fork/`pull_request_target` -> never checkout untrusted code in a privileged target-context workflow, split read-only build from separately approved write action (https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/); Action/tag compromise -> full-SHA pin, dependency review, workflow CODEOWNERS, minimal token, provenance, Scorecard/zizmor scans (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use; https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/); cache poisoning/persistent self-host contamination -> clean ephemeral image, trust-partitioned cache keys, no author cache, destroy after one job; script injection from PR title/body/branch -> pass untrusted values via environment/input, never interpolate into shell (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use).

Faults and recovery: duplicate/out-of-order/lost webhook -> event-id dedupe plus scheduled authoritative poll; stale lease/zombie writer -> heartbeat, expiry and monotonically increasing fencing token; force-push/head race -> exact-SHA CAS and invalidate evidence/review; same-named check spoofing -> ruleset required-workflow/source binding where available, unique job names and App identity; queue starvation/flakes -> timeout, quarantine labeled flakes, bounded infra retry, no “rerun until green”; merge conflict/base advance -> queue recomputation, return to EXECUTING/VERIFYING; artifact/log expiry -> retain compact signed manifest and digest separately; artifact tampering -> digest/attestation verification; Project drift -> dry-run diff/readback and `DRIFT_BLOCKED`; cleanup partial failure -> tombstone, retry with backoff, sweeper and human incident; branch name collision -> attempt UUID and repository ID; accidental active branch/worktree deletion -> verify terminal PR state, head SHA, lease owner and protected-ref denylist before deletion. Cancellation revokes credentials first, sends graceful stop, preserves bounded diagnostics, then force-destroys. Never delete security evidence under active incident/legal hold.
validation_and_tests:
Contract tests validate every JSON/YAML instance, reject unknown fields, and property-test legal/illegal state transitions, CAS, fencing, idempotency and monotonic terminal states. Replay fixture sequences for duplicate, delayed and reordered `pull_request`, `check_run`, `workflow_run`, `merge_group`, review, project and installation webhooks (payload reference: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads). Integration tests in a disposable GitHub organization/repository create real rulesets/App permissions/project fields, push two conflicting PRs, verify stale approval dismissal, verify a new head invalidates evidence, and prove required workflows run for `merge_group`; a canary intentionally omits the trigger and must be rejected as GitHub documents (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue).

Security tests submit shell metacharacters in titles/branches, malicious issue instructions, fork PRs, changed workflow files, symlinks, oversized artifacts, secret-like strings and cache collisions; assert zero secret/write-token exposure and run Scorecard/zizmor (https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md; https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor). Clean-room tests intentionally leave author-only files/cache/env/tool mutations and prove verifier cannot see them. Evidence tests alter source, manifest, artifact and workflow SHA independently and require rejection; attestations are verified offline where supported (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations). Cleanup chaos tests kill the controller between token revoke, worktree remove, ref/artifact deletion and Project update, then prove retry convergence without deleting live resources. Reconciliation tests cover missed webhooks, renamed/deleted/duplicate Project fields, unknown manual status edits, API 403/404/409/429/5xx and partial mutations; destructive or ambiguous drift must stop. Shadow and pilot evaluation manually labels AI-review true/false positives/negatives by severity and compares escaped defects, review time and rework; never promote solely on comment volume.
operational_maintenance:
Run three reconcilers: fast event handler, periodic authoritative poll, and daily garbage collector. Inventory leases, attempts, Git refs/PRs, worktrees/workspaces, check/workflow runs, Project items, bot comments and artifacts by stable IDs/tags. Cleanup order: freeze/revoke credential and lease; verify terminal/ownership/SHA; preserve compact audit/evidence and legal holds; `git worktree remove` then `prune`; delete disposable compute/cache; delete safe head ref; minimize/update rather than append bot comments; expire/delete large logs/artifacts per class; read back absence; mark `DONE`. Git explicitly distinguishes remove and prune (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree); GitHub exposes ref, artifact and workflow-run deletion endpoints/how-tos (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/git/refs; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/delete-a-workflow-run).

Dashboards: attempts by state/age, lease freshness, webhook lag/dedupe, Project drift, required-check/head mismatches, queue depth/latency/timeouts, flake/retry classification, review aging, token/permission denials, artifact retention, cleanup backlog/orphans and deletion errors. Alert on stale active lease, unverified merge-ready head, bypass use, policy/workflow change, secrets finding, unsigned release artifact, drift blocked >SLO, or cleanup retry exhaustion. Runbooks cover stale lease, queue outage, GitHub API/rate limit, compromised Action/token, artifact loss, Project drift, and restore from journal. Upgrade via pinned-dependency PR, schema migration with backward-compatible reader, dry-run fixtures/shadow repository, human approval and rollback. Comments are projections: keep one controller summary comment updated by marker/ID; never delete human discussion, approvals, security evidence or exception rationale. Large raw artifacts may expire, but preserve the manifest, hashes, verdict, source/workflow SHAs and retention/deletion audit.
maturity_and_uncertainty:
Maturity assessment: branch protection/rulesets, Actions checks, merge queue, Git worktree lifecycle, GitHub APIs and artifact retention are production-grade primitives; exact-head evidence manifests, split identities, event dedupe/CAS/fencing, cleanup sagas and Project drift reconciliation are established distributed-systems patterns but require custom engineering. Artifact attestations/SLSA integration is conditionally mature by artifact/ecosystem. AI code review is useful as advisory triage but remains conditional: an industrial paper reports 75% precision, and field evidence notes false-positive/risk/context concerns (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15134; https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16339). Fully autonomous merge based on AI review, automated semantic retry, and self-approved workflow/policy improvement are not supported.

High-confidence claims are the documented GitHub/Git/GITHUB Actions semantics and the need to test `merge_group`. Medium-confidence claims are the proposed controller boundaries, cleanup order and Project-as-projection model because they are architectural deductions. Low/unknown: local CI cost/latency, false-negative rate of AI/human review, queue behavior under this repository’s flakes, Project API eventual-consistency edge cases, artifact/legal retention, and whether GitHub features/limits differ by plan/Enterprise Server. The requested cutoff 2026-09-13 is future-relative to some cited versionless living docs and cannot be frozen from their pages; capture docs/API versions and revalidate platform behavior at implementation time.
implementation_recommendation:
MVP (proposal-only, 2–4 weeks): add schemas/lifecycle/risk/permissions/evidence/cleanup policy, CODEOWNERS and protected ruleset; install a least-privilege GitHub App; implement durable attempt journal + lease/fencing; provision disposable worktree/VM; open draft PR; run exact-head clean-room CI; upload manifest/digests; require independent human approval; merge only through queue; reconcile Project status; revoke/delete/sweep. First canary must prove `pull_request` and `merge_group` checks, stale approval invalidation, webhook replay and cleanup after injected crashes. Do not grant implementation workers merge, ruleset, Project-schema, workflow, secrets, deploy or deletion powers.

Stage 2: dependency/code scanning, SBOM and artifact attestation, signed release artifacts, protected base-fail/candidate-pass regressions, automated Project drift dry runs, Scorecard/zizmor, cleanup dashboards/SLOs. Stage 3: advisory AI review with calibrated labeled evaluation; allow conditional low-risk auto-merge only for narrow R0/R1 classes after ≥100 representative PRs or an agreed statistically meaningful sample, zero severe escapes/bypass violations, bounded rollback, and unchanged human gates for protected/high-risk paths. Stage 4: governed improvement proposals: telemetry -> candidate prompt/tool/workflow/policy change -> immutable eval corpus -> offline/shadow/canary comparison -> independent security/CODEOWNER/human approval -> pinned promotion -> monitored rollback. The proposer cannot edit the baseline, evaluator, required gate or promoter. Core decision: own a small deterministic controller and evidence contract around GitHub primitives; do not make the agent, a Project column, an AI approval, or a green PR-head check the authority.

conflicts: GitHub permits configurable Copilot APPROVE reviews, but its default is COMMENT and empirical LLM review precision is not perfect; resolve by keeping AI advisory during pilot and requiring independent human/CODEOWNER approvals for governed paths (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/request-a-code-review/use-code-review; https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15134). Merge queue can optionally group a PR whose individual check failed when the combined group’s final check passes, useful for intermittent failures, but that obscures per-PR signal; select “only merge non-failing pull requests” initially and classify flakes rather than relaxing evidence (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue). GitHub-hosted jobs are fresh VMs, while persistent self-hosted runners may retain state; “new job” and “clean room” are equivalent only on an independently rebuilt/ephemeral runner (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/github-hosted-runners; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/self-hosted-runners). Artifact digest validation proves transferred bytes match, and attestation proves a claimed build relationship; neither proves tests are adequate or the code correct. Status-as-code conflicts with mutable Project reality: repository YAML is desired configuration, GraphQL is actual state; solve with read/diff/apply/readback and block ambiguous/destructive drift (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects). Auto-delete branches improves hygiene but can destroy diagnostic context; retain immutable evidence/SHAs and honor incident/legal holds before ref deletion.
confidence: Overall: high for platform primitives and security constraints; medium-high for the recommended delivery architecture; medium for cleanup/reconciliation details until exercised; low for local performance and autonomous-merge outcomes. High: exact-head checks, stale-approval behavior, `merge_group` requirement, least-privilege token controls, worktree remove/prune, artifact APIs/digests—direct official sources. High: `pull_request_target` and third-party Action risks—documented exploit/incident evidence. Medium: five-identity split, Project desired/observed reconciliation and cleanup saga—strong deductions but no cited reference implementation was evaluated end to end. Medium: AI review is useful only as additive evidence—two 2025 studies support it, but systems, languages and outcome definitions differ. Unknown until pilot: reviewer false-negative rate, flake rate, queue throughput, evidence retention cost, API consistency/rate behavior, and whether ≥100 PRs is statistically sufficient for rare severe defects.
uncertain: GitHub documentation is continuously updated and several feature limits/availability vary by plan and GitHub Enterprise Server version; snapshot the selected plan/API schemas and rerun live contract tests before rollout.
The source set does not establish an end-to-end causal defect-reduction rate for AI review or autonomous low-risk merge. Local labeled pilots must measure false negatives and severe escapes.

Project v2 mutation/read-after-write consistency, webhook delivery timing, ruleset required-workflow identity binding, and merge-queue behavior under this repository's CI provider need live sandbox verification.
Evidence/log/comment/artifact retention periods require organization legal, privacy, incident-response and cost decisions; no universal retention period is recommended.
The exact clean-room guarantee of a self-hosted runner depends on image rebuild, tenancy, cache and credential implementation; a new runner job alone is insufficient.

The as-of date supplied is 2026-09-13, but living versionless web docs cannot prove no later or geographically staged behavior change; record retrieved content hashes in the implementation evidence bundle.
